questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the detection of nitrogen in an organic compound via Lassaigne's test:
Statement I: During sodium fusion, the organic nitrogen and carbon are converted into ionic sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$), which on boiling with ferrous sulphate in alkaline medium forms sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II), $\text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$.
Statement II: On acidifying the resulting alkaline mixture with concentrated sulphuric acid, some ferrous ions are oxidized to ferric ions, which react with ferrocyanide to yield a Prussian blue precipitate of ferric ferrocyanide, $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In Lassaigne's test, sodium metal is fused with the organic compound converting covalent nitrogen and carbon into ionic sodium cyanide: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NaCN}$. Boiling the sodium fusion extract with freshly prepared $\text{FeSO}_4$ in alkaline medium produces ferrous hydroxide, which reacts with cyanide ions to form sodium hexacyanidoferrate(II): $\text{Fe(OH)}_2 + 6\text{NaCN} \rightarrow \text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6] + 2\text{NaOH}$. Hence, Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Acidification with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ dissolves the basic hydroxides and oxidizes a portion of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ to $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ($3\text{Fe}^{2+} \rightarrow 3\text{Fe}^{3+}$). The $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions then react with hexacyanidoferrate(II) ions to produce the characteristic Prussian blue precipitate of iron(III) hexacyanidoferrate(II): $4\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$. Hence, Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): An organic compound containing sulphur produces a brilliant purple or violet coloration when treated with freshly prepared sodium nitroprusside solution in alkaline Lassaigne's extract.
Reason (R): Sodium sulphide ($\text{Na}_2\text{S}$) formed during sodium fusion reacts with sodium nitroprusside, $\text{Na}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]$, to generate the thionitroprusside complex ion, $[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). During sodium fusion, organically bound sulphur is converted into water-soluble sodium sulphide: $2\text{Na} + \text{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Na}_2\text{S}$. When sodium nitroprusside is added to this alkaline solution, an intense purple-violet coloration develops immediately, confirming sulphur. Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The chemical basis of this test is the coordinate ligand-exchange/addition reaction where sulphide ion combines with the nitroprusside core: $\text{Na}_2\text{S} + \text{Na}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}] \rightarrow \text{Na}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]$. The resulting pentacyanonitrosylferrate derivative contains the $[\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NOS}]^{4-}$ complex ion, which exhibits an intense charge-transfer violet band. Hence, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the detection of halogens in an organic compound containing nitrogen and sulphur:
Statement I: Prior to testing for halogens with silver nitrate solution ($\text{AgNO}_3$), the Lassaigne's sodium fusion extract must be boiled with concentrated nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$).
Statement II: Boiling with concentrated nitric acid decomposes $\text{NaCN}$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$ into volatile $\text{HCN}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gases, preventing the premature precipitation of white $\text{AgCN}$ and black $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. If an organic compound contains nitrogen or sulphur along with halogens, the fusion extract contains $\text{NaCN}$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$. If $\text{AgNO}_3$ is added directly without treatment, $\text{CN}^-$ and $\text{S}^{2-}$ interfere by forming precipitates. Hence, boiling with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ is a mandatory preparatory step. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ oxidizes and decomposes sodium cyanide and sodium sulphide: $\text{NaCN} + \text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NaNO}_3 + \text{HCN}\uparrow$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{S} + 2\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 2\text{NaNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$. If not expelled, $\text{Ag}^+$ forms white $\text{AgCN}$ (mistaken for $\text{AgCl}$) or black $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$ (masking $\text{AgX}$ entirely). Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the behavior of nitrogen-containing compounds in Lassaigne's test:
List I (Compound):
A. Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$)
B. Aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$)
C. Urea ($\text{NH}_2\text{CONH}_2$)
D. Benzenediazonium chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$)

List II (Observation in Lassaigne's Test):
I. Fails to form sodium cyanide because the molecule completely lacks carbon
II. Readily forms sodium cyanide and yields a positive Prussian blue test
III. Contains both carbon and nitrogen, thus producing a positive Prussian blue test
IV. Readily loses nitrogen gas as $\text{N}_2$ on gentle warming before sodium fusion occurs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
B) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
C) A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
D) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Compound A (Hydrazine). Hydrazine ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2$) contains nitrogen but no carbon atom. Therefore, it cannot synthesize sodium cyanide ($\text{NaCN}$) upon sodium fusion and fails the Prussian blue test (A matches I).
Step 2: Analyze Compound B (Aniline) and Compound C (Urea). Both aniline ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$) and urea ($\text{NH}_2\text{CONH}_2$) contain both carbon and nitrogen, forming $\text{NaCN}$ upon sodium fusion and yielding a positive Prussian blue coloration (B matches III, C matches II).
Step 3: Analyze Compound D (Benzenediazonium chloride). Diazonium salts undergo rapid thermal decomposition upon heating, expelling nitrogen as volatile $\text{N}_2$ gas before reacting with sodium metal, failing the standard fusion test (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Lassaigne's test for an organic compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur:
Statement I: If sodium metal is used in limited amount during fusion of a compound containing both nitrogen and sulphur, sodium thiocyanate ($\text{NaSCN}$) is formed instead of separate $\text{NaCN}$ and $\text{Na}_2\text{S}$.
Statement II: On adding ferric chloride to this acidified fusion extract, a blood-red coloration is observed due to the formation of $[\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$, with no Prussian blue precipitate.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. When both nitrogen and sulphur are present and sodium is insufficient to decompose the organic chain fully into discrete cyanide and sulphide salts, sodium reacts according to: $\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} + \text{S} \rightarrow \text{NaSCN}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. When $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions are added to the acidified extract containing $\text{SCN}^-$, the thiocyanatoiron(III) complex ion is formed: $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{SCN}^- \rightarrow [\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$. This complex displays an unmistakable deep blood-red coloration. Free cyanide ions are absent, so no Prussian blue is precipitated. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding laboratory tests for unsaturation in organic compounds:
Statement I: Decolorization of a reddish-brown solution of bromine in carbon tetrachloride ($\text{Br}_2/\text{CCl}_4$) without the evolution of hydrogen bromide gas indicates the presence of carbon-carbon multiple bonds.
Statement II: Baeyer's reagent is a cold, dilute, neutral or alkaline potassium permanganate solution that oxidizes alkenes to vicinal syn-diols while being reduced to a brown precipitate of manganese dioxide ($\text{MnO}_2$).
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. An electrophilic addition of bromine across a double or triple bond consumes $\text{Br}_2$ to yield a colorless vicinal dibromoalkane. Because addition does not release gaseous $\text{HBr}$ (which occurs in substitution), the disappearance of color confirms unsaturation. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Baeyer's reagent is formulated as cold, dilute ($1\%$) alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$. Alkenes undergo syn-dihydroxylation across the double bond to yield glycols, during which purple permanganate ($\text{MnO}_4^-$) is reduced to a brown precipitate of hydrated $\text{MnO}_2$. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Treatment of an aliphatic alcohol with ceric ammonium nitrate reagent produces a characteristic red coloration.
Reason (R): The alcohol molecule acts as an oxygen-donor ligand, replacing nitrate ions to form a red-colored alkoxy-substituted cerate(IV) complex ion, $[(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Ce}(\text{NO}_3)_4(\text{OR})_2]$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Ceric ammonium nitrate, $(\text{NH}_4)_2[\text{Ce}(\text{NO}_3)_6]$, serves as a standard diagnostic reagent for detecting alcoholic hydroxyl ($-\text{OH}$) groups. Addition of an alcohol causes the yellow solution to turn cherry-red. Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The yellow hexanitratocerate(IV) anion undergoes ligand displacement wherein alcohol molecules coordinate via their lone pair on oxygen, releasing nitrate ions and yielding a coordination complex: $(\text{NH}_4)_2[\text{Ce}(\text{NO}_3)_6] + 2\text{ROH} \rightarrow [(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{Ce}(\text{NO}_3)_4(\text{OR})_2] + 2\text{HNO}_3$. This complex exhibits intense red coloration due to ligand-to-metal charge transfer. Hence, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the detection of the phenolic hydroxyl group:
Statement I: Phenol reacts with neutral ferric chloride solution ($\text{FeCl}_3$) to yield an intense violet coloration due to the formation of the hexaphenoxidoferrate(III) complex ion, $[(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O})_6\text{Fe}]^{3-}$.
Statement II: Aliphatic alcohols such as ethanol produce an identical intense violet coloration when treated with neutral ferric chloride solution under the same conditions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
D) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Phenols possess an enolic/phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group bonded directly to an aromatic ring. With neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$, six phenoxide ligands coordinate to the iron(III) center: $6\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + \text{FeCl}_3 \rightarrow [(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{O})_6\text{Fe}]^{3-} + 3\text{H}^+ + 3\text{HCl}$. This complex imparts a characteristic violet color. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Aliphatic alcohols are significantly less acidic than phenols ($pK_a \approx 16-18$ vs $\approx 10$) and do not readily form stable coloured coordination complexes with neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$. Therefore, ethanol does not produce a violet coloration. Statement II is incorrect.
Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Brady's reagent (2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine):
Statement I: Both aldehydes and ketones condense with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine in weakly acidic medium to precipitate yellow, orange, or red crystalline 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazones.
Statement II: The condensation reaction involves a nucleophilic attack of the hydrazine amino group on the electrophilic carbonyl carbon followed by dehydration to yield a compound containing a $>	ext{C}=	ext{N}-$ bond.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Brady's test is a general test for the carbonyl functional group ($>\text{C}=\text{O}$). Both aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes and ketones react with 2,4-DNP to form brightly colored (yellow to red-orange) crystalline precipitates with well-defined melting points. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The reaction proceeds through nucleophilic addition of the terminal $-\text{NH}_2$ nitrogen of 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine to the carbonyl carbon, generating a tetrahedral intermediate, which subsequently loses a molecule of water via acid-catalyzed elimination to establish the $>	ext{C}=	ext{N}-$ (hydrazone) double bond. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Benzaldehyde ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO}$) forms a shining silver mirror on the inner walls of the test tube upon gentle warming with Tollens' reagent.
Reason (R): Tollens' reagent contains the diamminesilver(I) complex ion, $[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$, which acts as a mild oxidizing agent capable of oxidizing both aliphatic and aromatic aldehydes to carboxylate ions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Tollens' reagent is reduced by aldehydes to elemental silver ($	ext{Ag}^0$), which deposits as a reflective mirror or black precipitate on the clean glass surface: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHO} + 2[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COO}^- + 2\text{Ag}\downarrow + 4\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Tollens' reagent consists of an ammoniacal solution of silver nitrate containing the $[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$ cation. It is a sufficiently strong oxidant to convert both aliphatic aldehydes and aromatic aldehydes (such as benzaldehyde) into corresponding carboxylates, while remaining unreactive toward simple ketones. Hence, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Fehling's test:
Statement I: Aliphatic aldehydes like ethanal reduce Fehling's solution on heating to give a red precipitate of cuprous oxide ($\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$).
Statement II: Aromatic aldehydes like benzaldehyde readily reduce Fehling's solution to give a red precipitate of cuprous oxide under identical conditions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Fehling's solution (a mixture of aqueous copper sulphate and alkaline sodium potassium tartrate) oxidizes aliphatic aldehydes into carboxylate ions while cupric tartrate complex is reduced to cuprous oxide: $\text{R-CHO} + 2\text{Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O}\downarrow (\text{red}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Fehling's solution is a weaker oxidizing agent than Tollens' reagent. Because the carbonyl carbon in benzaldehyde is stabilized by resonance with the phenyl ring, it is less electrophilic and cannot be oxidized by Fehling's solution. Thus, aromatic aldehydes fail Fehling's test. Statement II is incorrect.
Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the structural requirements and observations in the iodoform (haloform) test with $\text{I}_2/\text{NaOH}$:
List I (Compound):
A. Propan-2-ol ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$)
B. Pentan-3-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$)
C. Acetophenone ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COCH}_3$)
D. Methanol ($\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$)

List II (Observation and Structural Criterion):
I. Forms yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ due to presence of $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group
II. Negative test because it lacks a $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ moiety
III. Forms yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ due to presence of $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ attached to benzene ring
IV. Negative test because it is a primary alcohol lacking the terminal methyl carbinol unit

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
B) A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
C) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
D) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Compound A (Propan-2-ol). Propan-2-ol contains the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ group, which is oxidized by hypoiodite ($\text{OI}^-$) to acetone and subsequently iodinated to produce a yellow precipitate of iodoform ($\text{CHI}_3$) (A matches I).
Step 2: Evaluate Compound B (Pentan-3-one). Pentan-3-one has the carbonyl group flanked by two ethyl groups ($-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$) and lacks the methyl ketone ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$) structure, yielding a negative iodoform test (B matches II).
Step 3: Evaluate Compound C (Acetophenone) and Compound D (Methanol). Acetophenone contains a methyl ketone group attached to phenyl, readily yielding $\text{CHI}_3$ and sodium benzoate (C matches III). Methanol is a primary alcohol without the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)}-$ unit, yielding a negative test (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the sodium bicarbonate test:
Statement I: Carboxylic acids react with saturated aqueous sodium bicarbonate ($\text{NaHCO}_3$) solution to produce brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide gas that turns lime water milky.
Statement II: Simple phenol ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}$) also produces brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide with aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$ solution because of its acidic character.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Carboxylic acids ($pK_a \approx 4-5$) are stronger acids than carbonic acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$, $pK_a \approx 6.4$). Therefore, they displace carbonic acid from sodium bicarbonate: $\text{RCOOH} + \text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\uparrow$. The liberated $\text{CO}_2$ gas produces brisk effervescence and precipitates calcium carbonate in lime water. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Phenol is a weaker acid ($pK_a \approx 10$) than carbonic acid. According to Bronsted-Lowry acid-base principles, a weaker acid cannot displace a stronger acid from its conjugate salt. Hence, phenol does not react with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ and produces no effervescence. Statement II is incorrect.
Conclusion: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): When aniline is heated with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide, an extremely offensive and foul-smelling vapour of phenyl isocyanide is evolved.
Reason (R): The carbylamine reaction is a specific diagnostic test given exclusively by primary amines (both aliphatic and aromatic) and proceeds via dichlorocarbene intermediate.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Aniline is a primary aromatic amine. Upon heating with chloroform ($\text{CHCl}_3$) and ethanolic $\text{KOH}$, it undergoes the carbylamine test: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 + \text{CHCl}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NC} + 3\text{KCl} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The product, phenyl isocyanide, is recognized by its intolerably foul odour. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Secondary and tertiary amines cannot form isocyanides because they lack two hydrogen atoms on the nitrogen atom. The reaction involves the generation of the highly reactive electrophilic intermediate dichlorocarbene ($:\!\text{CCl}_2$) from chloroform and base. Hence, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the behavior of amines in the Hinsberg test using benzenesulphonyl chloride ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$):
List I (Amine Class):
A. Primary aliphatic amine ($\text{R}-\text{NH}_2$)
B. Secondary aliphatic amine ($\text{R}_2\text{NH}$)
C. Tertiary aliphatic amine ($\text{R}_3\text{N}$)
D. Quaternary ammonium salt ($\text{R}_4\text{N}^+\text{Cl}^-$)

List II (Observation with Reagents):
I. Forms an N-alkylbenzenesulphonamide which dissolves in aqueous $\text{KOH}$ due to an acidic proton on nitrogen
II. Forms an N,N-dialkylbenzenesulphonamide which remains insoluble in aqueous $\text{KOH}$
III. Does not react with benzenesulphonyl chloride under ordinary alkaline conditions
IV. An ionic salt that remains completely unreactive toward benzenesulphonyl chloride

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Primary Amine (A). Reaction with $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{Cl}$ yields $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{NHR}$. The hydrogen attached to nitrogen is strongly acidic due to the electron-withdrawing sulphonyl group, allowing it to dissolve in aqueous $\text{KOH}$ to form a potassium salt (A matches I).
Step 2: Evaluate Secondary Amine (B). Reaction yields $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{SO}_2\text{NR}_2$. Because there is no hydrogen on the nitrogen atom, it is non-acidic and insoluble in aqueous alkali (B matches II).
Step 3: Evaluate Tertiary Amine (C) and Quaternary Salt (D). Tertiary amines lack replaceable hydrogen on nitrogen and do not form sulphonamides under these conditions (C matches III). Quaternary ammonium salts are already tetra-substituted ionic species that do not undergo nucleophilic attack (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the detection of the ammonium ion ($\text{NH}_4^+$) in Zero group analysis:
Statement I: Heating an ammonium salt with aqueous sodium hydroxide solution liberates pungent-smelling ammonia gas that turns moist red litmus paper blue and produces dense white fumes with a glass rod dipped in concentrated $\text{HCl}$.
Statement II: Nessler's reagent is an alkaline solution of potassium tetraiodomercurate(II), $\text{K}_2[\text{HgI}_4]$, which produces a brown precipitate of iodide of Millon's base with ammonium ions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In Zero group analysis, $\text{NH}_4^+$ is detected by heating the solid salt or its aqueous solution with $\text{NaOH}$: $\text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NH}_3\uparrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. The alkaline ammonia gas turns moist red litmus blue and reacts with $\text{HCl}$ vapours to form white microcrystalline airborne $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ fumes. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Nessler's reagent is prepared by mixing mercuric iodide, potassium iodide, and potassium hydroxide, forming $\text{K}_2[\text{HgI}_4]$. With trace $\text{NH}_4^+$, it yields a characteristic brown precipitate of the basic amino-mercuric complex iodide of Millon's base: $2\text{K}_2[\text{HgI}_4] + \text{NH}_3 + 3\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{Hg}-\text{O}-\text{Hg}-\text{I}\downarrow + 7\text{KI} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The white precipitate of lead(II) chloride ($\text{PbCl}_2$) obtained in Group I inorganic analysis dissolves on boiling with water and recrystallizes as shining golden-yellow needles upon cooling.
Reason (R): Lead(II) chloride has a significantly higher solubility in boiling water than in cold water, enabling its separation from insoluble silver(I) chloride and mercury(I) chloride.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
D) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Lead(II) chloride ($\text{PbCl}_2$) is precipitated as a white solid with dilute $\text{HCl}$. It dissolves in boiling water, but on cooling, it reprecipitates as colorless/white shining needles or crystals, NOT golden-yellow needles. (Golden-yellow spangles are formed when $\text{PbI}_2$ is dissolved in boiling water and allowed to cool). Hence, Assertion (A) is false.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The solubility product of $\text{PbCl}_2$ increases markedly with temperature ($K_{sp}$ increases from $1.7 \times 10^{-5}$ at $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $3.3 \times 10^{-3}$ at $100^\circ\text{C}$). This enables selective dissolution and separation from silver(I) and mercury(I) chlorides, which remain insoluble even in boiling water. Hence, Reason (R) is true.
Conclusion: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Group II cation analysis for copper(II) ($\text{Cu}^{2+}$):
Statement I: In Group II analysis, $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ is precipitated as black copper(II) sulphide ($\text{CuS}$) by passing $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas through the acidified salt solution containing dilute $\text{HCl}$.
Statement II: The washed black $\text{CuS}$ precipitate dissolves in hot $50\%$ $\text{HNO}_3$, and subsequent addition of excess aqueous ammonia produces a deep azure-blue solution of the tetraamminecopper(II) complex, $[\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In qualitative analysis, Group II cations are precipitated as sulphides by passing $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ in the presence of dilute $\text{HCl}$. Copper forms black copper(II) sulphide: $\text{Cu}^{2+} + \text{S}^{2-} \rightarrow \text{CuS}\downarrow$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The $\text{CuS}$ precipitate dissolves in moderately concentrated nitric acid: $3\text{CuS} + 8\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 3\text{Cu(NO}_3)_2 + 2\text{NO}\uparrow + 3\text{S}\downarrow + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$. When excess ammonia is added, light blue cupric hydroxide initially formed dissolves to give the intensely deep azure-blue coordination cation: $\text{Cu}^{2+} + 4\text{NH}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Cu(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Group III qualitative inorganic cation analysis:
Statement I: Prior to adding ammonium hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$), solid ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$) must be added in substantial excess to the solution.
Statement II: The common ion effect exerted by $\text{NH}_4^+$ suppresses the dissociation of weak base $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, reducing $[\text{OH}^-]$ so that only hydroxides with very low $K_{sp}$ (such as $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ and $\text{Al(OH)}_3$) precipitate.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In systematic cation analysis, Group III cations ($\text{Fe}^{3+}, \text{Al}^{3+}$) are precipitated as hydroxides using $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ in the presence of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$. Adding solid $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ first is essential to ensure adequate $\text{NH}_4^+$ concentration. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ is a weak base: $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$. The high concentration of $\text{NH}_4^+$ from fully dissociated $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ shifts this equilibrium strongly to the left. Consequently, the hydroxide concentration $[\text{OH}^-]$ is low enough to exceed the $K_{sp}$ of $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ ($10^{-38}$) and $\text{Al(OH)}_3$ ($10^{-33}$), but not the higher $K_{sp}$ of Group IV and V cations (e.g. $\text{Zn(OH)}_2$, $\text{Mn(OH)}_2$, $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$). Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the characteristic flame coloration observed in dry tests using a clean platinum wire moistened with concentrated $\text{HCl}$:
List I (Metal Ion):
A. $\text{Ba}^{2+}$
B. $\text{Sr}^{2+}$
C. $\text{Ca}^{2+}$
D. $\text{Cu}^{2+}$

List II (Flame Color):
I. Apple green
II. Crimson red
III. Brick red
IV. Bluish green / green flame

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
D) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze flame colors of alkaline earth metals and transition metals. Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ converts metal salts into volatile chlorides which vaporize in the non-luminous Bunsen flame and emit characteristic atomic emission wavelengths.
Step 2: Match each cation with its NCERT defined flame color:
- $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ imparts a persistent apple green color to the flame (A matches I).
- $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ imparts a dazzling crimson red flame color (B matches II).
- $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ imparts a brick red flame color (C matches III).
- $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ imparts a distinctive bluish-green or green-edged flame (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the gases evolved when dilute sulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) is added to solid sodium salts of anions:
List I (Anion):
A. Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$)
B. Sulphite ($\text{SO}_3^{2-}$)
C. Sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$)
D. Nitrite ($\text{NO}_2^-$)

List II (Gas Evolved and Confirmatory Property):
I. Colorless, odorless $\text{CO}_2$ gas that turns clear lime water milky
II. Colorless $\text{SO}_2$ gas with burning sulphur odour that turns acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ paper green
III. Foul rotten-egg smelling $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas that turns moist lead acetate paper black
IV. Pale brown pungent $\text{NO}_2$ gas that turns starch-iodide paper dark blue

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Anion A (Carbonate). $\text{CO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\uparrow$. $\text{CO}_2$ is colorless and odorless, precipitating white $\text{CaCO}_3$ in lime water (A matches I).
Step 2: Evaluate Anion B (Sulphite). $\text{SO}_3^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{SO}_2\uparrow$. $\text{SO}_2$ smells of burning sulphur and reduces orange dichromate to green chromic sulphate: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 3\text{SO}_2 + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{SO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$ (B matches II).
Step 3: Evaluate Anion C (Sulphide) and Anion D (Nitrite). $\text{S}^{2-} + 2\text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$, which reacts with lead acetate to form black $\text{PbS}$ (C matches III). $\text{NO}_2^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2$, which disproportionates to evolve brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas that oxidizes iodide to iodine, turning starch paper blue (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In redox titrations involving potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$), dilute sulphuric acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) is added to provide an acidic medium, whereas dilute hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) is strictly avoided.
Reason (R): Potassium permanganate oxidizes chloride ions of hydrochloric acid to chlorine gas ($\text{Cl}_2$), causing premature consumption of $\text{KMnO}_4$ and yielding inaccurate, abnormally high titre values.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Permanganate redox titrations require an acidic medium to allow reduction of $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ($n$-factor $= 5$) to $\text{Mn}^{2+}$. Dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is ideal because sulphate ions are inert toward oxidation by $\text{MnO}_4^-$. Dilute $\text{HCl}$ cannot be used. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Permanganate has a standard reduction potential ($E^\circ = +1.51\text{ V}$) sufficient to oxidize $\text{Cl}^-$ ($E^\circ = +1.36\text{ V}$) to $\text{Cl}_2$: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 10\text{Cl}^- + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{Cl}_2 + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Consequently, extra $\text{KMnO}_4$ is consumed by the acid itself, leading to a false higher titre volume. Hence, Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the detection of phosphorus in an organic compound:
Statement I: During detection of phosphorus, the organic compound is heated with an oxidizing agent such as sodium peroxide ($\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$), which oxidizes organically bound phosphorus to sodium phosphate ($\text{Na}_3\text{PO}_4$).
Statement II: The aqueous extract of the fusion mixture is boiled with concentrated nitric acid and then treated with ammonium molybdate solution, producing a canary-yellow precipitate of ammonium phosphomolybdate, $(\text{NH}_4)_3[\text{P}(\text{Mo}_{12}\text{O}_{40})]$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In qualitative detection of phosphorus, the organic compound cannot simply be fused with sodium alone to form a simple binary salt. Instead, it is heated strongly with sodium peroxide ($\text{Na}_2\text{O}_2$), an effective oxidizing agent: $\text{P} + \text{Na}_2\text{O}_2 \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Na}_3\text{PO}_4$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The fusion mass is extracted with water and boiled with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ to convert sodium phosphate to phosphoric acid: $\text{Na}_3\text{PO}_4 + 3\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 3\text{NaNO}_3$. On adding excess ammonium molybdate, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{MoO}_4$, a distinctive canary-yellow precipitate of ammonium phosphomolybdate forms: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4 + 12(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{MoO}_4 + 21\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow (\text{NH}_4)_3[\text{P}(\text{Mo}_{12}\text{O}_{40})]\downarrow + 21\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3 + 12\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the organic layer test for bromide and iodide using chlorine water and carbon tetrachloride ($\text{CCl}_4$), the non-polar organic layer turns orange-brown for bromide and violet for iodide.
Reason (R): Chlorine, possessing a higher standard reduction potential ($E^\circ = +1.36\text{ V}$) than bromine ($E^\circ = +1.09\text{ V}$) and iodine ($E^\circ = +0.54\text{ V}$), oxidizes $\text{Br}^-$ and $\text{I}^-$ to elemental $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$, which selectively partition into $\text{CCl}_4$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
C) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). In the layer test, chlorine water oxidizes halides in the acidified sodium fusion extract. The liberated halogens are extracted into the denser non-polar $\text{CCl}_4$ layer, where molecular bromine produces an orange-brown shade and molecular iodine gives an intense violet color. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Because $E^\circ(\text{Cl}_2/\text{Cl}^-) > E^\circ(\text{Br}_2/\text{Br}^-) > E^\circ(\text{I}_2/\text{I}^-)$, chlorine displaces bromine and iodine via redox reactions: $2\text{Br}^- + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{Br}_2 + 2\text{Cl}^-$ and $2\text{I}^- + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{I}_2 + 2\text{Cl}^-$. Non-polar halogen molecules ($\text{Br}_2, \text{I}_2$) have substantially higher solubility in non-polar $\text{CCl}_4$ than in polar water according to like-dissolves-like. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding distinctive qualitative tests for the phenolic hydroxyl group:
List I (Laboratory Test):
A. Liebermann's nitroso reaction
B. Phthalein dye test
C. Bromine water test
D. Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ test

List II (Reagents and Diagnostic Visual Transformation):
I. Phenol + $\text{NaNO}_2$ + conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ deep blue/green color, turns red on dilution, and turns blue again with excess $\text{NaOH}$
II. Phenol + phthalic anhydride + conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta}$ poured into dilute $\text{NaOH}$ yielding a bright pink/fuchsia coloration
III. Phenol + aqueous $\text{Br}_2$ yields an immediate white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol with an antiseptic odour
IV. Phenol + neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ yields a characteristic deep violet-purple complex ion

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
B) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
C) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
D) A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Test A (Liebermann's nitroso reaction). Phenol reacts with nitrous acid to form 4-nitrosophenol, which tautomerizes to mono-oxime of 1,4-benzoquinone. This condenses with another phenol molecule in concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form red indophenol, which in alkaline medium ($	ext{NaOH}$) turns intensely blue due to the resonance-stabilized indophenol anion (A matches I).
Step 2: Evaluate Test B (Phthalein dye test). Condensation of two molecules of phenol with one molecule of phthalic anhydride in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives phenolphthalein. When discharged into dilute $\text{NaOH}$, it forms the pink dianion (B matches II).
Step 3: Evaluate Test C and Test D. Bromination of activated phenol with aqueous bromine affords white 2,4,6-tribromophenol (C matches III). Neutral $\text{FeCl}_3$ coordinates with phenol to generate the violet hexaphenoxidoferrate(III) complex (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding laboratory reagents used to chemically distinguish between pairs of organic constitutional isomers:
List I (Pair of Isomers to Differentiate):
A. Propanal and Propan-2-one
B. Pentan-2-one and Pentan-3-one
C. Ethanol and Methoxymethane (Dimethyl ether)
D. Benzoic acid and Phenol

List II (Distinguishing Chemical Reagent and Positive Response):
I. Fehling's solution (forms red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$ precipitate only with the aldehyde)
II. $\text{I}_2 / \text{NaOH}$ (forms yellow crystalline $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate only with the methyl ketone)
III. Ceric ammonium nitrate / Sodium metal (gives brisk $\text{H}_2$ effervescence and red color only with the primary alcohol)
IV. Saturated aqueous $\text{NaHCO}_3$ (gives brisk effervescence of $\text{CO}_2$ gas only with the carboxylic acid)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
B) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
C) A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
D) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Differentiate Pair A (Propanal vs Propan-2-one). Propanal is an aliphatic aldehyde which reduces Fehling's solution to give a brick-red precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$, whereas acetone (propan-2-one) is a ketone and fails Fehling's test (A matches I).
Step 2: Differentiate Pair B (Pentan-2-one vs Pentan-3-one). Pentan-2-one has a terminal methyl ketone group ($\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$) that gives a positive iodoform test (yellow $\text{CHI}_3$), whereas pentan-3-one has internal ethyl groups and gives a negative test (B matches II).
Step 3: Differentiate Pair C and Pair D. Ethanol contains an active alcoholic $-\text{OH}$ group, which reacts with sodium metal to evolve $\text{H}_2$ and gives a red complex with CAN, unlike dimethyl ether (C matches III). Benzoic acid is sufficiently acidic to displace $\text{CO}_2$ from $\text{NaHCO}_3$, whereas phenol is too weak to do so (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the reactions of primary amines with nitrous acid ($\text{HNO}_2$):
Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ to form highly unstable alkyldiazonium salts, which rapidly decompose even in cold water to evolve nitrogen gas quantitatively along with alcohols, alkenes, and alkyl halides.
Statement II: Primary aromatic amines such as aniline react with nitrous acid at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$ to form benzenediazonium chloride, which when coupled with an alkaline solution of $\beta$-naphthol yields a brilliant orange-red azo dye.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Aliphatic diazonium ions ($[\text{R}-\text{N}\equiv\text{N}]^+$) lack resonance stabilization. Even at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$, they undergo immediate heterolytic cleavage of the $\text{C}-\text{N}$ bond to release stable $\text{N}_2$ gas and form carbocations, which react with water to yield alcohols and other rearranged products. The volume of $\text{N}_2$ evolved is quantitative (Van Slyke method). Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. In aniline, the diazonium group is stabilized by resonance with the aromatic ring ($	ext{C}_6	ext{H}_5-	ext{N}^+\equiv\text{N} \leftrightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5^+=\text{N}=\text{N}^-$), remaining stable in aqueous solution at $0-5^\circ\text{C}$. When treated with an alkaline solution of 2-naphthol ($\beta$-naphthol), electrophilic aromatic substitution occurs at the 1-position of naphthol, yielding the bright orange-red precipitate of 1-(phenylazo)-2-naphthol. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Cations of Group IV ($\text{Ni}^{2+}, \text{Co}^{2+}, \text{Mn}^{2+}, \text{Zn}^{2+}$) do not precipitate as sulphides in Group II analysis when $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas is passed in the presence of dilute $\text{HCl}$.
Reason (R): In acidic medium, the high concentration of hydronium ions from completely ionized $\text{HCl}$ suppresses the ionization of weak diprotic acid $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ via the common ion effect, maintaining $[\text{S}^{2-}]$ at a level too low to exceed the solubility products of Group IV sulphides.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
C) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
D) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). In systematic qualitative analysis, Group II cations ($\text{Cu}^{2+}, \text{Pb}^{2+}, \text{As}^{3+}$) are precipitated as sulphides with dilute $\text{HCl} + \text{H}_2\text{S}$, while Group IV cations remain in solution. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Hydrogen sulphide is a weak diprotic acid: $\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{H}^+ + \text{S}^{2-}$, with $K_a = K_1 K_2 \approx 10^{-21}$. Dilute $\text{HCl}$ provides a high $[	ext{H}^+]$ (around $0.2-0.3\text{ M}$). By Le Chatelier's principle and the common ion effect, this suppresses sulphide dissociation, holding $[\text{S}^{2-}] \approx 10^{-20}-10^{-22}\text{ M}$. This concentration is sufficient to exceed the extremely low $K_{sp}$ of Group II sulphides ($K_{sp}(\text{CuS}) \approx 10^{-36}$), but remains far below the ionic product required to precipitate Group IV sulphides ($K_{sp}(\text{ZnS}) \approx 10^{-24}, K_{sp}(\text{MnS}) \approx 10^{-13}$). Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding confirmatory tests for Group III cations:
Statement I: The gelatinous white precipitate of aluminium hydroxide dissolves in aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ due to the formation of soluble sodium tetrahydroxoaluminate(III), $\text{Na}[\text{Al(OH)}_4]$, and reprecipitates upon boiling with solid $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$.
Statement II: The reddish-brown precipitate of ferric hydroxide dissolves in dilute $\text{HCl}$ to form $\text{FeCl}_3$, which produces a deep Prussian blue precipitate with potassium ferrocyanide and an intense blood-red coloration with potassium thiocyanate.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. $\text{Al(OH)}_3$ is amphoteric: $\text{Al(OH)}_3 + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}[\text{Al(OH)}_4]$ (soluble sodium aluminate). When boiled with solid $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$, ammonium ions consume hydroxide ions ($	ext{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{NH}_3\uparrow + \text{H}_2\text{O}$), reducing the $\text{pH}$ and causing $\text{Al(OH)}_3$ to reprecipitate as a gelatinous white solid. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Reddish-brown $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ dissolves in dilute $\text{HCl}$: $\text{Fe(OH)}_3 + 3\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{FeCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. With $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$, it yields Prussian blue: $4\text{Fe}^{3+} + 3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} \rightarrow \text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3\downarrow$. With $\text{KCNS}$, it forms the blood-red thiocyanato complex: $\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{SCN}^- \rightarrow [\text{Fe(SCN)}]^{2+}$. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In Group IV qualitative inorganic analysis, nickel(II) ion is confirmed by the formation of a brilliant scarlet-red precipitate when treated with dimethylglyoxime in an ammoniacal solution.
Reason (R): The resulting bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II) coordination complex, $[\text{Ni(dmg)}_2]$, has a square planar geometry stabilized by two symmetrical intramolecular $\text{O}-\text{H}\cdots\text{O}$ hydrogen bonds.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). In Group IV, $\text{NiS}$ is dissolved in aqua regia or hot dilute $\text{HCl}/\text{KClO}_3$. The solution is buffered with $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ to slightly alkaline $\text{pH}$ and treated with ethanolic dimethylglyoxime. An intense, insoluble rose-red/scarlet precipitate forms immediately. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Two mononegative dimethylglyoximate mono-anions coordinate to the central $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ion (which undergoes $\text{dsp}^2$ hybridization to form a planar diamagnetic complex). The two ligands are linked together laterally by two exceptionally strong, short intramolecular $\text{O}-\text{H}\cdots\text{O}$ hydrogen bonds between the oxime oxygens, creating a highly rigid, uncharged, water-insoluble neutral chelate ring system. Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding confirmatory chemistry for Group IV cations:
Statement I: Zinc sulphide ($\text{ZnS}$) dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid; addition of $\text{NaOH}$ gives a white precipitate of $\text{Zn(OH)}_2$ which dissolves in excess $\text{NaOH}$ to yield soluble sodium zincate, $\text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2$.
Statement II: Manganese sulphide ($\text{MnS}$) dissolves in dilute hydrochloric acid; on boiling the solution with concentrated nitric acid and lead dioxide ($\text{PbO}_2$), a characteristic purple/pink supernatant of permanganic acid ($\text{HMnO}_4$) is formed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. White $\text{ZnS}$ dissolves in dilute $\text{HCl}$: $\text{ZnS} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$. Addition of $\text{NaOH}$ precipitates amphoteric $\text{Zn(OH)}_2$, which dissolves in excess $\text{NaOH}$ to form sodium tetrahydroxozincate(II) (commonly written as sodium zincate): $\text{Zn(OH)}_2 + 2\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{ZnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Buff-colored $\text{MnS}$ dissolves in dilute $\text{HCl}$ to give $\text{MnCl}_2$. Heating with strong oxidizing agent $\text{PbO}_2$ in concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ oxidizes $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ($+2$) to permanganic acid $\text{HMnO}_4$ ($+7$): $2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 5\text{PbO}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{Pb}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The purple color of permanganate confirms manganese. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the selective separation and confirmatory tests of Group V alkaline earth metal cations:
List I (Cation Separation Step):
A. Precipitation of $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ from acetic acid solution
B. Precipitation of $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ from the barium-free filtrate
C. Precipitation of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ from the strontium-free filtrate
D. Role of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ during Group V carbonate precipitation

List II (Reagent and Distinctive Chemical Basis):
I. Addition of potassium chromate ($\text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4$) yields a yellow precipitate of $\text{BaCrO}_4$ insoluble in dilute acetic acid
II. Addition of saturated ammonium sulphate, $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$, yields a white precipitate of $\text{SrSO}_4$
III. Addition of ammonium oxalate in ammoniacal solution yields a white precipitate of $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$
IV. Suppresses carbonate ion concentration via common ion effect to prevent the precipitation of $\text{MgCO}_3$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
D) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Analyze Step A (Barium separation). The Group V carbonates ($\text{BaCO}_3, \text{SrCO}_3, \text{CaCO}_3$) are dissolved in warm dilute acetic acid. Potassium chromate is added: barium chromate precipitates as a yellow solid because its $K_{sp}$ ($1.2 \times 10^{-10}$) is low enough to precipitate in dilute acetic acid, whereas $\text{SrCrO}_4$ and $\text{CaCrO}_4$ remain dissolved (A matches I).
Step 2: Analyze Step B and Step C. To the filtrate, saturated $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ is added to precipitate white $\text{SrSO}_4$ (B matches II). From the remaining filtrate, ammonium oxalate precipitates calcium as white $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$ (C matches III).
Step 3: Analyze Step D. $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ provides excess $\text{NH}_4^+$, repressing the ionization of $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$, keeping $[\text{CO}_3^{2-}]$ below the threshold for $\text{MgCO}_3$ precipitation (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding Group VI analysis for magnesium ion ($\text{Mg}^{2+}$):
Statement I: In Group VI analysis, magnesium ion is detected by adding disodium hydrogen phosphate ($\text{Na}_2\text{HPO}_4$) solution in the presence of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ and excess $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, which forms a white crystalline precipitate of magnesium ammonium phosphate, $\text{Mg(NH}_4)\text{PO}_4\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$.
Statement II: Scratching the inner wall of the test tube with a glass rod facilitates the rapid nucleation and crystallization of magnesium ammonium phosphate from the supersaturated solution.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In the filtrate obtained after removing Group V cations, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ is confirmed by adding $\text{Na}_2\text{HPO}_4$ in ammoniacal medium containing $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$: $\text{Mg}^{2+} + \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{PO}_4^{3-} + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Mg(NH}_4)\text{PO}_4\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}\downarrow$. The resulting precipitate is white and microcrystalline. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Magnesium ammonium phosphate readily forms supersaturated solutions that crystallize slowly. Vigorous scratching of the glass walls with a glass rod creates minute microscopic glass surface abrasions that act as heterogeneous nucleation sites, initiating rapid crystallization of the white solid. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): When a solid mixture of sodium chloride and potassium dichromate is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid, deep reddish-brown vapours of chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) are evolved.
Reason (R): Heavy metal chlorides such as mercury(II) chloride ($\text{HgCl}_2$) and silver chloride ($\text{AgCl}$) also readily respond to the chromyl chloride test under identical experimental conditions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). In the chromyl chloride test, solid ionic chlorides react with solid potassium dichromate in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$: $4\text{NaCl} + \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 + 6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\uparrow + 4\text{NaHSO}_4 + 2\text{KHSO}_4 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The deep reddish-brown volatile liquid chromyl chloride vaporizes immediately. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Chlorides of heavy metals like $\text{HgCl}_2, \text{Hg}_2\text{Cl}_2, \text{AgCl}, \text{PbCl}_2,$ and $\text{SnCl}_2$ are covalent or sparingly soluble, and do not generate significant chloride ion concentrations to form chromyl chloride. Therefore, they fail to give the chromyl chloride test. Hence, Reason (R) is false.
Conclusion: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the brown ring test for the detection of nitrate ions ($\text{NO}_3^-$):
Statement I: The brown ring formed at the liquid-liquid junction is composed of the coordination complex pentaaquanitrosyliron(I) sulphate, $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]\text{SO}_4$, in which iron is in the $+1$ oxidation state.
Statement II: The presence of bromide ($\text{Br}^-$) or iodide ($\text{I}^-$) ions interferes with the brown ring test because concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ oxidizes them to colored halogens ($\text{Br}_2$ or $\text{I}_2$), obscuring the observation of the ring.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In the ring test, nitrate is reduced by $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ in acidic medium to nitric oxide: $\text{NO}_3^- + 3\text{Fe}^{2+} + 4\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 3\text{Fe}^{3+} + \text{NO} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The unreacted $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ binds $\text{NO}$ to form $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})]^{2+}$. In this complex, electron transfer from $\text{NO}$ to $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ yields $\text{Fe}^+$ ($d^7$, $S=3/2$) and coordinated $\text{NO}^+$ (nitrosonium), giving iron an oxidation state of $+1$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. When concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is added down the sides of the tube, bromide and iodide are oxidized to reddish-brown $\text{Br}_2$ or violet $\text{I}_2$ vapor/solution at the junction. Furthermore, nitrites ($\text{NO}_2^-$) form a brown ring even with dilute acid without concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. Hence, halides and nitrites seriously interfere with the nitrate ring test. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Match List I with List II regarding the independent group anions (sulphate and phosphate) and their confirmatory reactions:
List I (Anion and Confirmatory Reaction):
A. Sulphate ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) with aqueous $\text{BaCl}_2$ solution
B. Sulphate ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) with lead acetate solution
C. Phosphate ($\text{PO}_4^{3-}$) with ammonium molybdate in conc. $\text{HNO}_3$
D. Phosphate ($\text{PO}_4^{3-}$) with magnesia mixture

List II (Precipitate Formula and Characteristic Solubility):
I. White precipitate of $\text{BaSO}_4$ insoluble in concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$
II. White precipitate of $\text{PbSO}_4$ soluble in warm ammonium acetate solution
III. Canary-yellow precipitate of $(\text{NH}_4)_3[\text{P}(\text{Mo}_{12}\text{O}_{40})]$
IV. White crystalline precipitate of $\text{Mg(NH}_4)\text{PO}_4\cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
B) A-I, B-III, C-II, D-IV
C) A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
D) A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Sulphate Tests (A and B). $\text{BaCl}_2$ produces white $\text{BaSO}_4$, which has an extremely low solubility product and is completely insoluble in concentrated mineral acids like $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HNO}_3$ (A matches I). Lead acetate produces white $\text{PbSO}_4$, which dissolves in ammonium acetate solution due to the formation of soluble lead acetate complexes or un-ionized lead acetate (B matches II).
Step 2: Evaluate Phosphate Tests (C and D). Heating phosphate with concentrated $\text{HNO}_3$ and ammonium molybdate yields a canary-yellow precipitate of ammonium phosphomolybdate (C matches III). Treatment with magnesia mixture ($\text{MgCl}_2 + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) gives a white crystalline precipitate of magnesium ammonium phosphate (D matches IV).
Conclusion: The correct matching sequence is A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the borax bead test:
Statement I: When crystalline borax ($\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7\cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$) is heated on a platinum wire loop, it loses water of crystallization, swells into a porous mass, and ultimately fuses into a clear, transparent, glassy bead composed of sodium metaborate ($\text{NaBO}_2$) and boric anhydride ($\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$).
Statement II: In the borax bead test, copper compounds form a blue bead of cupric metaborate, $\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$, in the oxidizing flame, but in the luminous reducing flame, the bead turns red and opaque when cold due to the formation of metallic copper.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. On heating, borax loses its ten molecules of water of crystallization: $\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7\cdot 10\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 + 10\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Further strong heating causes decomposition and fusion: $\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7 \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{NaBO}_2 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3$. This homogeneous glassy melt forms the transparent bead. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. In the non-luminous oxidizing flame, $\text{CuO} + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$ (blue bead). In the reducing flame containing carbon and carbon monoxide: $2\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2 + 2\text{C} \rightarrow 2\text{CuBO}_2 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 + 2\text{CO}$ (colorless when hot), and further reduction: $2\text{CuBO}_2 + \text{C} \rightarrow 2\text{Cu} + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 + \text{CO}$, producing an opaque red bead of finely divided metallic copper upon cooling. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the selection of indicators in acid-base volumetric titrations:
Statement I: In the titration of a weak acid (such as acetic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) against a strong base (such as $\text{NaOH}$), phenolphthalein (pH range $8.3-10.0$) is a suitable indicator, whereas methyl orange (pH range $3.1-4.4$) cannot be used.
Statement II: At the equivalence point of a weak acid-strong base titration, the salt formed undergoes anionic hydrolysis to generate a basic solution ($\text{pH} \approx 8.5-9.0$), where the steep vertical inflection on the titration curve overlaps with the transition range of phenolphthalein.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
C) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
D) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. In weak acid-strong base titrations, the equivalence point lies entirely in the alkaline region ($	ext{pH} > 7$). Phenolphthalein changes color precisely in this range ($8.3-10.0$). Methyl orange changes color between $\text{pH } 3.1-4.4$, which occurs before the equivalence point is reached, leading to premature and inaccurate end points. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. The salt sodium acetate hydrolyzes according to: $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{OH}^-$. The $\text{pH}$ at the equivalence point is given by $\text{pH} = 7 + \frac{1}{2}pK_a + \frac{1}{2}\log C \approx 8.7$. The sharp pH inflection region ($7.5$ to $10.0$) coincides with phenolphthalein's visual transition interval. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): In the titrimetric estimation of oxalic acid with standard potassium permanganate ($\text{KMnO}_4$), the conical flask is warmed to $60-70^\circ\text{C}$ prior to titration, and the initial decolorization of permanganate is sluggish but accelerates rapidly as the titration proceeds.
Reason (R): The redox reaction has a high activation energy at ambient temperature, and the $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ ions generated as a product act as an autocatalyst, drastically lowering the activation barrier for subsequent reaction steps.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
C) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). The reaction: $2\text{MnO}_4^- + 5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 10\text{CO}_2\uparrow + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is exceedingly slow at room temperature. Heating to $60-70^\circ\text{C}$ provides sufficient kinetic thermal energy to initiate the reaction. The first 1-2 drops of $\text{KMnO}_4$ take tens of seconds to decolorize, after which successive drops decolorize almost instantaneously. Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). The initial uncatalyzed step involves mutual repulsion between negatively charged $\text{MnO}_4^-$ and $\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}$ anions, creating a high activation barrier. As soon as trace $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ is produced, it forms intermediate complexes with oxalate (e.g. $[\text{Mn(C}_2\text{O}_4)_2]^-$ and $\text{Mn}^{3+}$), providing an alternate pathway of much lower activation energy (autocatalysis). Reason (R) is true and correctly explains Assertion (A).
Conclusion: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Consider the following two statements regarding the laboratory preparation and electrical charge of lyophobic colloidal sols:
Statement I: Ferric hydroxide sol is prepared by adding $2\%$ $\text{FeCl}_3$ solution dropwise into boiling distilled water, and the colloidal particles acquire a net positive charge due to the preferential adsorption of $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions.
Statement II: Arsenious sulphide sol is prepared by passing $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas through a boiling aqueous solution of arsenious oxide ($\text{As}_2\text{O}_3$), and the colloidal particles acquire a net negative charge due to the preferential adsorption of sulphide ($\text{S}^{2-}$) or bisulphide ($\text{HS}^-$) ions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
B) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
C) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
D) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Statement I. Ferric hydroxide sol is synthesized by hydrolysis: $\text{FeCl}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{boiling}} \text{Fe(OH)}_3(\text{sol}) + 3\text{HCl}$. According to Paneth-Fajans-Hahn adsorption rule, the precipitated $\text{Fe(OH)}_3$ particles preferentially adsorb common $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ ions from unhydrolyzed $\text{FeCl}_3$, forming a positively charged Stern layer: $[\text{Fe(OH)}_3]\text{Fe}^{3+}$. Statement I is correct.
Step 2: Evaluate Statement II. Arsenious sulphide sol is prepared by double decomposition: $\text{As}_2\text{O}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow \text{As}_2\text{S}_3(\text{sol}) + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The colloidal $\text{As}_2\text{S}_3$ particles preferentially adsorb common sulphide ions ($\text{S}^{2-}$ or $\text{HS}^-$) present in excess from dissolved $\text{H}_2\text{S}$, forming a negatively charged sol: $[\text{As}_2\text{S}_3]\text{S}^{2-}$. Statement II is correct.
Conclusion: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The enthalpy of neutralization of dilute hydrochloric acid ($\text{HCl}$) with dilute sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) is $-57.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$, whereas the enthalpy of neutralization of dilute hydrocyanic acid ($\text{HCN}$) with dilute $\text{NaOH}$ has a magnitude significantly less than $57.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ ($\Delta H = -12.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$).
Reason (R): Strong acids and strong bases are completely ionized in dilute aqueous solutions so their neutralization is simply the combination of $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{OH}^-$ ions to form $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, whereas $\text{HCN}$ is weakly ionized and part of the heat released during neutralization is consumed in the complete ionization of $\text{HCN}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
B) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
C) Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
D) Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Evaluate Assertion (A). Enthalpy of neutralization is the enthalpy change when one equivalent of acid is neutralized by one equivalent of base in dilute aqueous solution. For any strong acid-strong base pair, $\Delta H_{\text{neut}} = -57.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. For weak acids such as $\text{HCN}$ ($pK_a = 9.2$), the measured enthalpy of neutralization is only $-12.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ (magnitude $|\Delta H| = 12.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \ll 57.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Assertion (A) is true.
Step 2: Evaluate Reason (R). Strong acid and base dissociation is complete ($100\%$), hence the net ionic reaction is universally $\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{OH}^-(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$, $\Delta H^\circ = -57.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
